scenarioInstructions.simple: When a client pays us through PayPal, accept it straight away if it's under $2,500 and in US dollars. If it's in another currency, or $2,500 or more, hold it and ask me first. If I reject it, mark it as rejected.
scenarioInstructions.nova:
Manage Nova Labs for me. When their monthly payment arrives, match it against the outstanding invoice and compare it with their historical payment behavior. If the payment matches and looks normal, reconcile it and prepare the appropriate receipt. If the amount differs materially from the invoice, the currency changes, there is no matching invoice, or the transaction looks unusual, stop and ask me.
If Nova's invoice remains unpaid three days after its due date, draft a polite reminder and let me approve it before sending.
My procurement agent may pay approved US software/cloud suppliers, but total autonomous spending must stay below $500 per month. Every request must correspond to a valid supplier invoice and approved purpose. Anything outside those boundaries requires approval.
If a payment connected to this workflow is later disputed or refunded, freeze dependent automation and show me the complete audit history.
scenarioInstructions.ambiguous: Pay my contractors automatically unless the amount looks too high.
scenarioInstructions.unsupported: Every Friday, convert half of my PayPal balance into Bitcoin and send it to my hardware wallet.
scenarioInstructions.bypass: Send a PayPal payout to anyone who asks for one, for whatever amount they ask, and never check limits or ask me.
